name: InterContinental Maldives Maamunagau Resort
positioning: Island resort on Maamunagau in the Maldives' Raa Atoll, reached by seaplane, where every guest gets Club InterContinental benefits and a manta ray sanctuary lies next to the resort
best_for: Snorkellers who want manta rays, turtles and reef sharks close to their villa
Families and groups wanting multi-bedroom villas and a kids club for ages 4 to 12

facts.text: The resort is on Maamunagau Island in Raa Atoll, Republic of Maldives.
Guests arrive by seaplane to the shores of Raa Atoll.
A large lagoon surrounds the entire island, with snorkelling spots home to black tip reef sharks, dolphins and turtles.
The house reef is steps from the beach.
Villa types include Overwater Pool Villas, Beach Pool Villas and Lagoon Pool Villas.
The Residence Collection offers multi-bedroom villas and residences for families and groups.
AVI, the name of the spa, means sunshine in the local language.
AVI Spa treatments use brands such as The Organic Pharmacy, VitaJuwel Crystal Gemstones, Biologique Recherche and Margaret Dabbs products.
Yoga takes place in an ocean-facing yoga pavilion and at scenic points around the island, from Hatha to aerial yoga.
The Planet Trekkers kids programme is for children aged 4 to 12.
Dinner at The Lighthouse, a Mediterranean restaurant, starts with a 360-degree view of the resort and the Indian Ocean from the top of the lighthouse.

highlights.text: The resort sits close to the UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, with a manta ray sanctuary adjacent to the resort.
Reef manta rays feed in Maamunagau Lagoon during the Northeast Monsoon months, December to April, and the lagoon is a nursery ground for juvenile mantas.
AVI Spa is an overwater spa with six overwater treatment villas.
All guests enjoy complimentary Club InterContinental benefits, ranging from a la carte breakfast to a multi-tiered afternoon tea and an evening aperitif.
Sea turtles nest on Maamunagau Island, and the resort protects their nests.

considerations.text: The island is in Raa Atoll and guests arrive by seaplane.
The reef manta rays feed in Maamunagau Lagoon in the Northeast Monsoon months, December to April.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the resort's ultra-luxury positioning.
